description: CustodyComms Update Manifest - Controls forced updates and version requirements

forceUpdate._doc: appliesTo NAMES WHO THIS FORCE UPDATE IS FOR, as <process.platform>-<process.arch> keys. A client whose platform/arch cannot fetch a listed target is NOT blocked. It is REQUIRED whenever enabled is true: from v2.0 on, a forceUpdate block with no appliesTo is treated as FORCE_UPDATE_NO_SCOPE_DECLARED and blocks nobody. That is deliberate — the force-update window is closable:false, so blocking a client that has no artifact to fetch is an unrecoverable lockout with no server-side rollback. See update/release-targets.js. WARNING: clients at v1.9.0 and below SHIP THE OLD GATE AND IGNORE THIS FIELD ENTIRELY — raising minVersion above what those clients can install locks every one of them out regardless of what is written here.
forceUpdate._lock: O-12 (LOCKED-DECISIONS-2026-09-03.md:56): force-update is OFF for the v2.0 cut; the ordinary optional update prompt is the only thing users see. enabled:false is the lock. Do NOT flip this to true as part of a version bump — it is an owner contract change, and frontend/tests/update/force-update-arch-gate.test.js pins it to false so the flip cannot land silently. minVersion/appliesTo/severity/message are kept in their documented shape so the block stays a template, not a fragment.
forceUpdate.message: Important sign-in + security fix: 1.9.0 finishes closing the sign-in recovery loop that affected some users on prior versions, and adds a multi-tenant data-isolation hardening pass on the AI incident-analysis routes. Recommended for all users; 1-day grace before the update becomes mandatory.

features._doc: Remote feature flags. Parsed by update-manager.js (this.manifest.features) and exposed to the renderer via update:get-features → window.appConfig.features. OPS KILL SWITCH: set a flag to false here to dark the corresponding UI surface for all clients on the next manifest fetch — no redeploy. navigator_chat=false darks the Matter Builder 'Ask the AI' live-chat engine (MatterBuilderRailModule.navigatorChatEnabled); the frontend probe ALSO fails closed on any error. NAVIGATOR-CHAT-CUT (owner 2026-09-13): navigator_chat is FALSE at the cut and MatterBuilderRailModule.navigatorChatEnabled() is default-OFF to match — the two must move together, and scripts/cut-mac-update-release.sh refuses the cut unless this key is exactly false. Turning it back on ships an interactive AI chat the owner declined; it is not a cosmetic toggle. NOTE what it does NOT gate: the 'Your guide' panel. Since MB-GUIDE-INFORMATIONAL (0cc90d6a) the panel is matter-builder-render.guide() in EVERY flag state, so darking this flag does not dark the panel. FIX-WHOS-WHO-EXISTING-1014: whos_who_fix=false hides every Fix who's who entry point (the Matter Setup button and callout, the attention banner; window.WhosWhoFix.isEnabled). Default true. It is a renderer switch only: the authenticated POST /api/v1/cases/{uuid}/participants/whos-who stays live (the UI is the only door, a stated residual on the desktop trust boundary).

highlights: Quick Start: drop in a message file and CustodyComms brings it in and finds your incidents. Matter Builder (Beta) builds the whole matter with you, step by step.
Evidence Library: your documents and photos, beside your messages. One exhibit can now hold messages, documents and photos together.
Overview shows where a matter stands, on one page. Order Rules lets you write down what your parenting order says, in your own words, and connect incidents to it.
Sign in with Apple or Google. When you share a matter, you choose whether it includes pictures and whether to also send the whole original files.
Imports now ask you, or refuse and explain, instead of quietly guessing. Incidents you write yourself now survive a re-scan.
Message times name their time zone and print in the order they were sent. If a file doesn’t say its zone, the app asks you once. Older times it can’t place say “(time zone not recorded)”.

Your exported documents have changed: a rewritten certification page with a chain-of-custody affidavit, and custody page times marked “(UTC)”. An export may not match a v1.9 export, so re-export and compare.
Quick Start and Matter Builder now show who they found in each file before saving anything. Match a nickname, phone number or email to the right person with one click, or start over.
If a matter matched the wrong people, Matter Setup now has Fix who’s who to put it right.
Quick Start and Timeline now show each incident’s full AI analysis, as Matter Builder and Messages do.
Exhibit binders now finish on Windows. Before this update, every binder export on Windows stopped with an error.
Exports whose name contains an emoji now finish on Windows.

Sign-in recovery loop — root-cause fix. Closes the catch-22 where clicking a session-health step-up prompt could leave you locked out (one customer was stuck for 6h47m on 2026-05-05). The banner now distinguishes step-up prompts from sign-out and writes a deterministic force-login marker that survives reload and never depends on Firebase storage being clean. Sentinel marker is now structured JSON with a 7-day TTL and fails closed when unreadable.

Multi-tenant data isolation — AI incident analysis routes now case-scope every database lookup. Closes a defense-in-depth gap where colliding incident IDs from the demo seeder could in theory let one user's AI prompt include another user's messages. Existing tenant data was never exposed in production-observed traffic; this is hardening, not a remediation.

Demo-seeder collision fix. New users no longer share incident-group IDs across cases (root cause of the AI-isolation issue above). Existing colliding rows are deduped automatically on first launch with a pre-migration backup retained for 7 days.
Per-user AI concurrency cap. One Deep AI run at a time per user (returns 409 instead of stacking). Prevents memory pressure on machines running multiple analysis tabs.
App session heartbeat. New 5-minute beacon (`app_session_heartbeat`) lets us measure active-time-by-state without back-deriving from suppression accumulator math. Telemetry-only, no UI change.
Defense-in-depth on the menu Sign Out button — now writes the same sign-out sentinel the banner does, closing a previously-unprotected Firebase storage resurrection path.

Closes the sign-in recovery loop affecting some long-session users on 1.8.5–1.8.8: the app now renews your backend session token automatically on 401, instead of falling back to a working-but-stale Firebase auth and re-emitting the loop on every poll. Sixteen users on prior versions had this background loop firing every ~3 minutes; the fix targets the proven code path.

Stronger security on session refresh: on token-replay, device-mismatch, or refresh-token-expired failures, the app now clears all credentials and routes you to login (previously some of these fell through to a generic error).
Backend hardening: refresh no longer auto-renews step-up verification. Refresh is token rotation, not identity re-verification.
New telemetry events (auth_backend_refresh_attempted/succeeded/failed) so we can confirm the fix is firing in production for affected users.

Fixed a sign-in recovery loop affecting users with degraded local sessions — the app now recognizes when verification is required and shows a clear prompt instead of silently retrying. Resolves customer reports from 2026-04-25.
Step-up verification screens now keep your session 'pending' on disk, so a brief idle period or app reload doesn't kick you back into the loop.
Token refresh scheduler now stops itself if your local session goes bad — no more hourly retries on a broken state.
Build pipeline now verifies fix markers in the shipped artifact before signing — prevents another 'fix shipped but didn't reach users' scenario.
Improved telemetry: every event now reports app_version so we can confirm rollouts hit users.
Fixed connection issue introduced in 1.8.6 that prevented backend from starting
All v1.8.6 sign-in and session recovery improvements included

Fixed a sign-in issue introduced in 1.8.5 that left some users with a blank matters list and no way to recover. The app now detects and breaks out of the loop, and surfaces a clear sign-in prompt if anything goes wrong.
Trusted-device sign-in is now persistent — once a step-up sign-in succeeds on this machine, you stay signed in across launches without needing to re-verify each time.
New 'Copy diagnostic' button in the sign-in error banner — share a privacy-safe diagnostic with support without leaking tokens or personal info.
